nodes.text: This fool grew more distressed day by day; he kept his
misery within himself and dared to no one
show his trouble. At last he found a sorcerer, a conjurer,
a devil's man who boasted greatly of knowing
the black art. To him he promised great sums
of money so that he might accomplish his will. Then
he began to practise his spells and called to
himself a devil who in the night-time should tempt the nun
and inflame [her] to sin and unchastity. The devil came to
her cell door; there stood St Jerome's image, painted
on the door. See here, my dear lord Augustine, what
power God has given his servant St Jerome:
for where his image is, the devil cannot come near,
so that wherever anyone is tormented by the devil, [if] there comes
St Jerome's image, the devil flees from there.
